hero.headline: Four arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen and pursuit, deputies say
hero.teaser: Four suspects were arrested in Martin County following an armed robbery of a teenager and a subsequent pursuit, according to deputies.
hero.body:
Four people accused of armed robbery of a teenager were arrested after a pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies. The arrests followed the incident involving the teen victim.

Deputies arrested the four suspects after the pursuit concluded in Martin County. The case involves an armed robbery and a chase that led to the arrests Monday.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound getting first Aldi grocery store at former Winn-Dixie site on July 9
cards.body:
Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi store when the new grocery store opens July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road. The location is in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be.

Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years. The Hobe Sound location marks the discount grocer's latest expansion in the region.

A grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony will be held July 9 at 8:30 a.m. The first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card.

The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. The new store brings a different grocery option to the Hobe Sound community following the closure of the Winn-Dixie at that location.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds dominates Florida GOP governor debate he refused to attend
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds skipped Florida's first major Republican gubernatorial debate Thursday night, yet his name was invoked at least 60 times by the three candidates who showed up. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins, and businessman James Fishback each used the two-hour event to argue they represent the strongest alternative to the Trump-backed frontrunner.

Moderator Patrick Bet-David opened by calling Donalds "the elephant not in the room." He said he had urged Donalds to attend, but Donalds' position was that he has raised roughly $100 million and is polling between 48% and 58%. Bet-David summarized Donalds' response: "Till then, I'm not showing up" until another candidate hits double digits. Collins attacked the absence directly, saying "We don't do kings in the United States of America. We sure don't do them in Florida." He added that if Donalds wants the governor's mansion, "you've got to grow a spine, you've got to stand up, and you've got to fight for the people of Florida." Renner called Donalds' absence disrespectful and said "Every voter in this audience, everyone watching, everyone in the state deserves a debate." He argued Donalds is avoiding the stage because he cannot prove he is better qualified. Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising with his own ground game, saying Donalds may have made history raising money, but "our campaign made history by being the first campaign in Florida running for governor to visit all 67 counties." Donalds told WPLG previously, "If the race was close, and we were battling it out, we would be debating right now."

The debate centered on affordability, property taxes, insurance and hyperscale data centers. Fishback went furthest on taxes, saying "I don't support relieving your property taxes. I don't support reforming your property taxes. I support one thing, and one thing only, and that is completely and totally abolishing property taxes in the state of Florida." He promised to take a "chainsaw" to local government spending. Collins said cities and counties have "a spending problem" and need more accountability. Renner said the current property-tax amendment does not go far enough, pitching his "Florida First" plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting more burden to tourists, out-of-state investors and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers. Fishback promised to "reject and remove every experimental data center" in Florida. Renner said he would call a special session to stop hyperscale projects. Collins urged local control with state "guardrails," prompting Fishback to mock his answer as a "word salad."

The debate gave all three candidates clips and a chance to pressure Donalds over skipping the stage. Renner leaned on his record as House Speaker, Collins on his military service and role in the DeSantis administration, and Fishback on outsider energy. With Donalds still holding the polling, fundraising, and endorsement advantages, Thursday night looked less like a campaign-changing showdown and more like an audition, with three candidates trying to prove which one deserves a one-on-one fight with the frontrunner.

cards.headline: Four suspects arrested after armed robbery of teen and pursuit in Martin County
cards.teaser: Four people accused in the armed robbery of a teenager were arrested following a pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies.
cards.body:
Martin County deputies arrested four suspects accused in an armed robbery of a teenager after a pursuit. The arrests followed the robbery incident involving the teen victim.

Deputies pursued the suspects before taking them into custody. The four individuals now face charges related to the armed robbery case.

cards.headline: Trump intervened with FIFA president before Balogun red card suspension lifted
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after Folarin Balogun's red card, asking FIFA to review the decision before the suspension was lifted for Monday's World Cup match against Belgium.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American forward Folarin Balogun, calling FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the game to request a review of the red card Balogun received for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 2-0 round of 32 win on Wednesday. The red card had triggered an automatic one-game suspension. Trump later posted on social media thanking FIFA for reversing what he called a great injustice. FIFA announced Sunday that the suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match against Belgium on Monday, with the implementation suspended for a probationary period of one year.

The extraordinary move appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished by the decision, and Belgium coach Rudi Garcia mocked FIFA's action by comparing it to an April Fools' Day joke. Balogun, 25, has three goals in the tournament and plays for Monaco. He was born in Brooklyn to Nigerian parents who were living in London and in 2023 opted to change his national team affiliation from England. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino said the team was punished enough by playing with 10 men for 30 minutes against Bosnia-Herzegovina in a decision he called completely unfair.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Construction Begins on 18-Hole Golf Course at Esplanade at Solaeris in Port St. Lucie
cards.body:
Construction has started on an 18-hole golf course at Esplanade at Solaeris, a new golf residential community in Port St. Lucie being developed by Taylor Morrison. The course is designed by Ken Wilczynski.

The Esplanade at Solaeris development represents a new golf-focused residential project in Port St. Lucie. Taylor Morrison is building the community around the golf course amenity.

Wilczynski's design will shape the layout and character of the 18-hole course. The golf course construction marks a significant phase in the overall community development.

The project adds to Port St. Lucie's inventory of golf communities. Taylor Morrison continues to expand its presence in the Treasure Coast residential market with this golf-centered development.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while connecting local and international artists.
cards.body:
The nonprofit organization operates in the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once lived there. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks on it. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character, keeping it 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there.

The estate gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds. From the seven, the estate now has over 100. One beloved peacock named Bob is believed to be 60 years old and is recognizable because he walks with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. Art director Krystal Masters leads the art lab, which offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one sessions for complete beginners in various mediums like sculpting and watercolor.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram images of four syringes showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video showing her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena said she was heartbroken to withdraw and did everything she could but her knee was not ready to compete.

Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, telling fans to stay tuned to a city near them. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare with 3-2 extra time World Cup win
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in South Florida, advancing to the Round of 16 after the tiny island nation challenged them until the final minutes of extra time.
cards.body:
The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal in the 29th minute, and Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia in their World Cup debut.

Argentina advanced to face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappe in the Golden Boot race, and has extended his record with 12 goals during his eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football sets sights on state championship after 10-2 season
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for a state title run during the fall 2026 season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district title. A second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players, and the majority came from the middle school program. Robertson said the players know how things are run and have had a lot of success in their careers. He hopes their senior year is the best season the program has had. The veteran senior class has prompted the Scots to schedule more challenging opponents this fall.

Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level, which led to creating a challenging schedule for this year. He said the goal is to compete and reach that next level by playing against really good teams, which will also help attract new people to the program. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs. He said while the team wants to go undefeated in the season, that does not matter if they keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts give the team something to look forward to each day. He said working harder will allow them to see positive results when the season comes and break their record.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the return of the Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach this November. The event marks its 18th year bringing seafood and entertainment to the Treasure Coast.

The annual festival has become a fixture in Vero Beach, drawing visitors from across the region for food and family activities. Additional details about dates, location and vendors are expected to be released closer to November.
